verdict: OK to lend in Belagavi sugar and ethanol, but only to integrated mills with distillery capacity and clean cane-payment records; avoid pure-standalone mills leaning on an MSP revision that has not been notified.
title: Belagavi Sugar & Ethanol: a note to the credit manager
narrative: Cost is dominated by cane price, which is politically set and paid within days; revenue is sugar and ethanol sold over months. That mismatch is the whole credit story. **So when a proposal lands, check the split between sugar and ethanol revenue and the cane payment cycle first; if cane arrears exceed one fortnight, ask why before reading anything else.**

## Where cash and value sit now
**The local news is about price, not about demand: growers are agitating for a higher fair remunerative price and a higher sugar MSP, and the minister who owns mills says factories can pay more only if the Centre raises MSP [1][2][3].** That is a squeeze signal, not a growth signal. Peer results show the other side: Triveni reports improved profitability and reduced debt on strong sugar and distillery margins [5], and EID Parry lifted average realization to INR 51.2 per kilogram from INR 43.7 per kilogram on premium mix [6]. **So pursue mills that already earn a premium or ethanol margin; avoid those whose entire repayment case is an MSP increase that has not been notified.**

## The growth opportunity to pursue
**Karnataka's local demand backdrop is strong: GST collections up 11.1% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1%, and electricity demand up 23.3% against 9.5% [D].** For this industry that means power and ethanol offtake, not sugar alone. Rating commentary says remunerative ethanol prices and interest subvention for debt-funded distillery capex help prevent cane arrears piling up, and that ethanol offsets cyclicality for integrated mills [10]. **So target integrated mills adding distillery capacity, and cogeneration units selling to the grid; avoid standalone sugar mills with no diversification and no captive cane base.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the season, not the year: a cash-flow cycle that peaks at crushing and troughs before the next crush needs a limit sized to one season's cane bill, with repayment tied to sugar and ethanol receipts.** Take monthly: cane crushed and recovery rate, cane paid versus cane due, sugar stock and free stock, ethanol dispatch volumes, and quarterly the debt-service cover. **If cane arrears cross one fortnight, ask for the farmer payment schedule and hold new limits; if ethanol realizations fall below the level in the sanction note, reprice.** Rating reports show gearing near 1.4 times and interest cover around 2x for a rated peer [11]; use that as the outer edge, not the target.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the cane price negotiation, not the balance sheet: an agitation that blocks highways in Belagavi and Chikkodi [3] delays crushing and pushes arrears up before any ratio moves.** Second, watch whether MSP revision stays a demand [1][2] rather than a notification. Third, watch recovery rate and sugar stock ageing. **If crushing starts late or recovery drops, ask for a revised season cash flow before the next disbursement.** Note the rating sources carry no clear dates and some are from 2024 [9][11]; treat their ratios as directional only, and collect current gearing and cane arrears from the customer.
